[b]Code[/b]:
This week, we implemented shooting of ranged weapons for the new combat system. There are 4 different shoot modes:
[list]
[*] Charged: The shot is charged up by holding the left mouse button and is fired when releasing it. Speed and damage get scaled depending on how much the shot was charged. This mode will be used for bows.
[*] Semi-Charged: Similar to charged with the difference being, if the shot is not fully charged, it counts as a normal shot. This mode will be used for energy weapons which can fire powerful charged shots that use up more ammo.
[*] Semi-Auto: Standard one left click, one shot mode. This mode will be used for handguns.
[*] Full-Auto: The weapon will keep shooting as long as you hold down the left mouse button. This mode will be used for rifles.
[/list]
In addition to the shoot modes, we implemented reloading as well as an overheat feature. If a weapon overheats, you will not be able to shoot until it has cooled down again. Only some weapons can overheat (e.g. energy weapons).
On a different note, we have been experimenting with and started implementing upscaling technologies (DLSS, FSR and TSR), as well as their frame generation capabilities. While upscaling will not make a meaningful difference in CPU bottlenecked areas (like story mode at the moment), graphically intense sandbox scenes or playing on higher resolutions will have a positive impact on performance when upscaling is enabled.

[b]Character[/b]: 
The male fantasy sexy armor outfit is almost ready, once the model has been implemented for some Sethro-based characters we will transfer it over to some other models, too. This week we implemented aiming behavior for the new combat system. The behavior will, for the most part, be like the old system.
On top of that, we made a bunch of small tweaks and improvements to the already existing features of the new combat.
On the sandbox side, we have added another in-game tutorial; this time for Lights.

Animation Sequences supports bone controllers now
UI Int/Float/Text fields have font size options now
Added user tooltips to UI props
Added 9-slice option to image prop
Added an event receiver to Lua prop to open the code editor
Added wl_character_get_num_outfits Lua function

[b]Animations[/b]:

[b]Design[/b]:
We have added 20 new collectable plants to be distributed over the different biomes of the world. Some of these serve as simple ingredients for meals, some can be used for fine delicacies that have a high trading value, and last but not least there are rare alchemy ingredients like the Fury Blossom, which when combined with hunting trophies from dangerous monsters make powerful potions that can swing the course of a fight drastically.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41311107/c02ac23d4284739a1aad429ef49b4aa7c9a2264e.jpg[/img]
Materials can be collected from world objects like ore veins and plants or looted from enemies. They can then be used to improve weapons and armor pieces. Since the different factions have varying technology levels, certain gear requires specialized NPCs to be upgraded. Plasma rifles, power fists or state-of-the-art combat armor can be improved by a tinkerer, while warrior or cannibal weaponry requires an old school smith. Tailors are specialized in refining non-combat designated clothing like dresses, casual garments or even lingerie.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41311107/8de615a0c0212c1030bcd73ef00b401eaee96d56.png[/img]
We also started working on a new quest for Max with Iljah de la Gourmand. A galactic gourmet, who follows the expedition to experience the different tastes of the universe and reliably gets into trouble while doing so.

Speaking of armor, that feature was implemented this week, as well. The armor items make use of the outfit system to display on the character, so there are 5 armor slots as well (head, chest, hands, legs, feet). The armor stats of each equipped piece get added together for the total armor rating.
In addition to that, we implemented quick slot functionality for weapon and armor items. This allows you to quickly equip and unequip them via the quick slot system. 
The quick slot radial menu received some love, as well.
On the sandbox side, one new tutorial (Event example: Door) was added, explaining the basic setup on how to make interactable doors. We also started work on an animation sequence tutorial explaining how the editor works.

Buy prices and sell prices vary between traders and can be changed via quests. notes.title: Our goals for 2024 + Development Update 19.01.2024
notes.content:
Hey everyone,

We hope your year is off to a good start. In this post we want to communicate our general goals for 2024.

[b]Combat System[/b]

One of the first things we will be tackling is the combat system. Our design team will clear the last questions and then code and animation will be implementing and finalizing the whole thing and we will be blocking out sound and visual effects for the combat system.

This is one of the last big elements we are still missing to have the game be fully playable in terms of systems. Our goal for this year is to have a fairly polished human x human and human x monster combat ready so this will include us finishing all the animations required for this for both humans and monsters.

[b]Movement Animation System[/b]

Along with that we will also be concentrating on the character movement animation system. Under the hood it has bloated considerably and it's time we clean it up, simplify it, improve its editability for animation and finish the last remaining features such as the swimming and grappling hook.

[b]NPC Routines[/b]

For the world to feel more alive, one of the most important tasks will be to finalize and implement NPC routines with routine destinations and animations. So the world can have plenty of spots for its inhabitants to work, sleep and relax.

[b]Level Art[/b]

We are aiming for blockouts of all locations to reach B state and bring 50% of locations to A state after that. For a better description of what A and B blockout states are, check last week's 2023 summary. The landscapes of the world will also be in focus of our efforts to move to a look that better resembles the final result. This includes:
[list]
[*] Finishing all rocks, cliffs, and mountain models and textures.
[*] Final placement and new iteration for water material of all rivers and lakes.
[*] Fully dressing the complete game world with blockout plants and trees.
[*] Having the main space-ship designs and blockouts ready, including the Blackrock and Federation landers.
[/list]
[b]Character Art[/b]

The faction and NPC outfits will also reach completion by mid-2024 and the NPC body models will be completed by the end of the year.

We also want to re-work and finalize the character skin material with its final feature list. This includes things like better wetness effects, tattoos, dirt layers and customization. This should be an improvement in both performance and looks!

[b]Sex Minigames[/b]

Sex content is one of the aspects Wild Life isn't really lacking, but of course we will continue to produce nice animations. We are still missing around 7 sex minigames and our main focus will be to flesh out the Maya x Max romance. Naturally we will be constantly adding new animations to the sandbox viewer.

[b]Story Mode[/b]

We plan to fully implement the game’s main-story quests and reach at least 80% of the side-quest implementation and sex-minigame integration as well as design and blockout 80% of the game world’s mini-locations (such as caves, campsites, ruins, etc.).

We also want to finish item design for all items and implement them in the game at least with blockout models. This includes things like consumables, weapons, routine items and quest items. Monsters and their spawning logic will also be something that our designers will be figuring out so exploring the world has some challenges too.

[b]Performance[/b]

Performance is always on our radar and this year we plan to make several performance-improving adjustments to the game both in art and code. We want to look into VRAM usage, optimizing material setups, texture management and nanite improvements in the art department and various game-system optimizations in code.

[b]Sandbox[/b]

Last but not least, the Wild Life sandbox will of course continue to be improved, features added and new content implemented.

We are looking forward to this year to finally see the world of Wild Life reach a state that could be considered a playable game.

notes.title: SUMMARY 2023 and Overall Progress Report
notes.content:
2023 was quite the eventful year, with lots of challenges and setbacks but also considerable progress. Today we want to share a little recap of last year, as well as an overview of the general state of development for Wild Life.

Last year started very tough, with the update to UE5 and all the issues that came with it, such as the missing fur, the changed physics system and the unexpectedly low performance, we knew it wouldn't be an easy year. While our coders were mainly busy with managing the engine version update, our designers were working hard on implementing the quests for the main story. But not only that, they also made significant progress in designing, writing and implementing many of the side quests.

On the art side, things moved at a very satisfactory pace. We completed the entire design for our faction and NPC outfits and our freelance artists turned many of these beautiful outfits and characters into reality.

The world map has been iterated in accordance with the main story, and most of the important locations needed for the plot have already been established in blockout. We also worked on designs for the plants and trees in the world and developed the pipelines to populate it with the models.

Most of the sex minigames needed for our main- and side quests are already animated and will be gradually integrated into the story mode. Our talented animators also worked on the NPC routine animations, creating some by hand and polishing mocap data for others.

Performance is always a very prominent aspect of development and we have been working hard to improve it, but of course there is still a lot to do. A few months ago, we took the opportunity to analyze the project for its performance potential with the help of a professional team of game performance analysts. The result is a promising list of areas where we can make improvements. Unfortunately, some optimization work can only be carried out at a later date, so we humbly ask for your patience. Nevertheless, our goal will always be to reach the best possible performance for the game.

The sandbox got some very impressive additions last year and we are quite proud of its current state. Of course this is a very important game mode of Wild Life and we will continue to work on it based on your input.

The darkest chapter of 2023 is without a doubt the discord hack which we experienced in May. This event has deeply affected and shaken us, as we had invested a lot of time and effort into the old server. Losing it from one day to the next was extremely stressful and caused us a lot of anxiety. However, thanks to the support of our community, we were able to set up a new Discord server within 24 hours and are very happy to see it's better than ever. We have since made many changes to how we handle security to prevent such a thing from happening again. We would like to take this opportunity to thank everyone for their support, especially in that trying period.

Looking forward to 2024 fills us with a positive energy and motivation. Next week we will share an outlook into what we have planned this year in all departments.

Once again we want to thank all of you for the invaluable support you have given.

-Wild Life Team

notes.title: Wild Life - Sandbox with UE4 is Now Free on Steam!
notes.content:
Hello everyone! Here at Candy Valley Network, we have been working hard on Wild Life, an innovative adult RPG that seamlessly integrates two engaging game modes which are both currently in development and evolving:

[u][b]Wild Life - The Game[/b][/u] - An immersive RPG experience that draws you into an expansive world, brimming with endless possibilities!

[u][b]Wild Life - Sandbox[/b][/u] - Your playground to create! Import your assets, construct unique environments, and generate narratives that resonate with your imagination!

The game still has a long journey until we feel that it is ready to be fully released on Steam. We know that will take a lot of time, but we want to deliver an amazing adult RPG, that is our goal! 

Still, we agree that news and updates about the game's progress should be frequent here, and we wanted to bring more of the game to Steam in some shape or form, especially with all the updates that were made during its development cycle on Unreal Engine 4! That said.....

[b]We are happy to announce that Wild Life - Sandbox 2022 UE4 is entirely free on Steam![/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41311107/3166d614e40757b27b07527e6fac2cb2677af956.png[/img]
[h3]What is Wild Life - Sandbox with Unreal 4?[/h3]

Step into a richly detailed world of limitless exploration, interaction, and expression with our Unreal 4 release! Immerse yourself in a realm of stunning possibilities and tailored experiences unlike any other.

[list]
[*] Dive into over 1,000 high-end sex animations, creating a cosmos of sensual combinations at your fingertips.
[*] Craft your unique narrative with 50+ distinctive characters paired with character customization - your design, your rules.
[*] Dress for success, seduction, or anything in between with 50+ unique outfits.
[*] Satiate your desires, no matter how niche or mainstream, with our extensive range of kinks.
[*] Build your dream world with our detailed sandbox editor. Share your masterpiece with friends and community members on Discord.
[/list]
Since our 2021 demo on Steam, we've dedicated ourselves to refining and expanding upon these game modes, driven by our commitment to offering an unrivaled adult experience.

This Sandbox version is an absolute beast and a treasure trove of content. It offers a more profound glimpse into the unique experiences that the Wild Life community has to offer - and we're making it accessible for everyone on Steam!

Today, we're replacing our 2021 Steam demo with the latest complete build we released on our crowdfunding campaign at the end of 2022!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41311107/c911480cf7f7e2a05cb776162ad5a75bc9bd9dcd.png[/img]
[h3] Unreal 5 and Future Updates on Steam[/h3]

While our current supporters are enjoying the most recent builds, developed with Unreal Engine 5, we wanted to invite those yet to join our adventure. This updated version on Steam invites you to experience Wild Life, and we're confident you'll be enticed to explore further!

Our supporters will keep receiving updates on Unreal 5 as they are delivered on our crowdfunding page. On Steam, the next update will take time, because it will be the full game release, including all updates and improvements that were and will be made during the game development cycle.

[h3]Dev Blogs now on Steam[/h3]

With this new step that we took for Steam, we will fix an issue that we made: the lack of communication about the game development! To clear any misunderstandings, these dev blogs were being released typically, but only on our social media, crowdfunding page, and Discord. 

Now they will also be available on Steam! While these blog updates will primarily focus on the builds supported by our current crowdfunding supporters, we aim to ensure you stay informed about the game's development, as all the additions and enhancements will ultimately contribute to the Steam release as well.

So, come and step into the world of Wild Life, it is waiting for you to shape it, your world, your rules!

Make sure to join our [url=discord.gg/TueZKjsfjW]Discord[/url], check our [url=https://docs.google.com/document/d/1AwNmy2ra3Uo4koiUGxPdsaZ7x1DmV0uHuov8h5Syn6g/edit]Sandbox tutorial document[/url] and engage with the Wild Life Community!
